title: If the sea were ink
hook: if every tree were pens and the sea ink, with seven more seas, His words would not run out (31:27)

segments.voice: Yesterday, walk modestly, and your line was lower your voice. Where were you usually loudest, and what happened at half the volume? Day five hundred thirty-six.

Before printing, writing was physical. A calligrapher cut a pen from a reed, sharpened it with a knife, dipped it, wrote a few words, dipped again. Ink was ground and mixed by hand, and it ran out. A copy of the Qur'an could take months. Every scribe knew the feeling of the pot running dry halfway through a line. Surah Luqman, near its end, takes that ordinary scribe's experience and stretches it until it breaks.
screen: `A REED PEN, A KNIFE, A POT OF INK.`

segments.voice: Pickthall: "And if all the trees in the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven more seas to help it, (were ink), the words of Allah could not be exhausted. Lo! Allah is Mighty, Wise." Try to picture it. Every tree on earth, every forest, every orchard, every palm, cut into pens. The aqlam, the reed pens. Then the ocean as the ink pot. Then seven more oceans poured in behind it. And the scribes write, and write, and the pens wear down, and the seas go dry, and the words of God are still not finished. Pickthall puts were ink in brackets because the Arabic leaves it out; the picture is so clear it doesn't need saying. The Qur'an has a shorter version of the same image in Surah Al-Kahf: if the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would run out before His words did, even if We brought another like it. What are the words? Commentators gave several answers. His knowledge, which has no edge. His commands, the be! by which everything comes into being. His wonders in creation, which no one could ever finish describing. Seven, in Arabic, often works as a number of abundance, not a precise count. The verse isn't measuring; it's overwhelming. And it makes something clear about every book, every sermon, every lesson, including this one. They're a few drops from that sea. Whatever has been said about God, there's always more. That isn't a frustration. For many Muslims it's a comfort: the source never runs dry.
screen: `EVERY TREE ON EARTH, A PEN.` · `THE SEA, AND SEVEN MORE, AS INK.` · `HIS KNOWLEDGE, COMMANDS AND WONDERS.` · `A FEW DROPS FROM THAT SEA.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: write one word of praise. Sit, and let the breath settle. Find a pen and a scrap of paper, or picture one. Think of one thing in the world that amazes you. The color of a sky. A child's laugh. The way a wound closes. Write one word for it, or one short line about God's work in it. Look at the word. Notice how much more there is that you didn't write. Let that feel like abundance, not failure. If you pray, you can say subhan Allah over it. The bell holds the time.
Aqlam. Pens: Luqman's picture of every tree becoming one, and the sea, with seven more, as ink, and the words of God still not running out. Today's word.
Your line: the words don't run out. Today, keep the scrap with your word on it, and add one more word before you sleep. Day five hundred thirty-six.

howItsDone: Muslims often recite 31:27 and 18:109 when speaking of the vastness of God's knowledge and words, and calligraphers have written the verse many times.

original.note: Arabic: pens, the plural of qalam, the reed pen; the trees become aqlam in 31:27.

trapdoor: what you thought: God knows a lot.
what it means: every tree as a pen and the sea, with seven more, as ink would run out before God's words; every book is a few drops from that sea.
what a scholar hears: aqlam and 'seven seas' in 31:27, paralleled in 18:109; commentators read kalimat as His knowledge, His commands ('be!'), and His wonders.

sources.quoted: And if all the trees in the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven more seas to help it, (were ink), the words of Allah could not be exhausted. Lo! Allah is Mighty, Wise.

notes: Pickthall 31:27 quoted from memory; confirm wording and bracket.
Commentators' readings of kalimat (knowledge, commands, wonders) summarized; confirm.
'Seven' as a number of abundance in Arabic idiom: commonly noted by commentators; confirm.
Audit: the word segment and trapdoor said 'eight seas', contradicting the script's own myth that the verse isn't counting; both now say 'the sea, with seven more'.
